sentences.text: Bambolinetta lignitifila is an extinct waterfowl species known from Late Miocene deposits in Italy.
The only known specimen is a partial skeleton containing an incomplete skull, most of the trunk, a right wing, and parts of the leg bones, representing a mid-sized duck.
This bird possessed arm bones, particularly the humerus, that were much stouter than those of any other ducks, and its ulna was short relative to the humerus and hand.
Its arm bones were significantly stouter than those of any other ducks, and the short ulna resembles features seen in auks and penguins.
Scientists consider it a highly unusual, likely flightless, wing-propelled diver similar to a penguin.
Alessandro Portis formally described the species in 1884 under the name Anas lignitifila.
Gerald Mayr and Marco Pavia conducted the first reexamination of the species in a 2014 paper, establishing the genus Bambolinetta based on its type locality.
The sole specimen is a partial skeleton collected in Montebamboli, Tuscany.
The parent group of Bambolinetta is the subfamily Anatinae, and it belongs to the family Anatidae.
Fossils of Bambolinetta date to the Late Miocene epoch, specifically the Aquitanian stage from 23.04 to 20.45 million years ago, when the region formed the Tusco-Sardinian island.
